title: A pitched adjacency lying flat beneath a deck hands a FALLING body to the world below, velocity and per-body register intact
binding: Two hand-authored documents under real separate authorities, colocated in one process the way seamless-four-corners-circuit is: island.world.json is a 12x12 deck at y=120 whose one adjacency lies FLAT 40 m beneath it (center 0,80,0 outwardYawDegrees 0 outwardPitchDegrees -90, 90x90), and corner.world.json owns everything below that plane through the reciprocal +90 face over its own floor at y=76. The positive leg proves four things the sky island's rim needs. (1) A pitched boundary validates and its reciprocity is proven off disk: world.adjacencies echoes 'pitch=-90 size=90x90' and a derived overlap of 3.0172, so outwardPitch -90 means outward-is-down and the owned half-space is ABOVE the plane, with width spanning the frame's Right (world +X) and height its Up (world +Z). (2) The body walks off the deck and is handed over WHILE AIRBORNE: the engine's own transfer narration carries the arrival read-back inline at pos y=79.09 with facts=airborne|falling and home=(0.00, 76.03, 0.00) — the corner's spawn, so the read is on the corner's authority — proving the hand-off is neither refused for an airborne body nor re-grounded on arrival, and that the carried vertical velocity survives (WorldFrameIsometry.MapArrival). (3) Per-body action state crosses: a Grounded-edge kit trigger adds 3 to the 'stamina' counter on every grounding, so 6 on the corner side is the island's grounding plus the corner's — the register file crossed the seam rather than resetting to its authored initial. (4) The arrival settles on the CORNER's own floor at y=76.03, a fixed point. Every asserted number is either engine-emitted at the crossing tick or a settled fixed point, and every counter is advanced by a kit action on exact simulation ticks; world.wait only has to be long enough, so a loaded host's catch-up burst cannot move any verdict. The seam's two faces point at each other — outward yaw 0/pitch -90 above, outward yaw 180/pitch +90 below — so the arrival map is the identity: the body walks to z=-13.54 on the island and arrives at z=-13.54 still facing yaw 0, directly beneath the point of fall, with the echo's own turn=0 read-back naming the untwisted seam and threshold=0.6867 naming the vertical ownership deadband in force — one authority step of the kit’s own fastest vertical travel (40 u/s at 60 Hz) plus contact skin, which is also how far past the plane the hand-off waits. A flat pair authored at one yaw on both sides instead carries a half turn (WorldFrameIsometry's own invariant: the arrival turn is destinationYaw - sourceYaw - 180), and the arrival keeps its exact x because the neighbour's frozen record still shows the traveler at the slot it departed from, and a seam's contact declines that one entity by its address (the rim-round-trip canary crosses the same seam three times and pins it on every leg). The discriminating leg boots island-solo.world.json, the same document with its references/destinations/adjacencies removed, and runs the SAME script: world.adjacencies reads 'none', no crossing and no arrival is narrated, the body leaves the deck and is still airborne|falling far below the island under its own authority, and stamina stays at 3 because it never touches ground a second time.
